transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, I'm here because my head just feels really foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things, which is getting frustrating. Like, uh, appointment times, or the dates for exhibits. I'll even forget which volunteer I already called and who I haven't spoken to yet. It's just been very hard to keep my thoughts straight.
How long have you been experiencing this foggy feeling in your head?
It's been going on for about four months now. It started right around the time we had some water damage, which ended up pushing us into doing a remodel.
Have you noticed any difficulty remembering things that happened before the water damage and remodel?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My memory for things in the past is... well, it's perfectly fine. It's really just the recent things, the day-to-day stuff happening right now, that I keep losing track of.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things?
No, not really. I mean, if I'm sitting down to read or watch a program, I can pay attention just fine. It's really just the remembering part that's giving me trouble.
Have you been having trouble organizing your daily tasks or activities?

No, not really. I manage to keep my days pretty organized. I know what I need to do and I get it done. It's just... well, like I said, it's just remembering the little things that happen during the day that seems to be the problem. But getting things organized? No, that's fine.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or depressed lately?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, I haven't been feeling sad or... depressed. My spirits are fine, really. It's just the frustration with my memory lately, but other than that, my mood is perfectly okay.
Are you having trouble learning new things, like a new skill or information?

No, I haven't noticed any trouble with that. I mean, I'm not exactly going out and trying to learn a bunch of new skills at my age, but... if someone explains something new to me or I need to figure out how to do something, I can pick it up just fine. It really just comes back to the memory thing I mentioned. But learning itself? No, that seems okay.
Do you find yourself having to relearn information that you already knew, such as passwords or phone numbers?
No, I don't think so. I haven't had to relearn anything like that. I mean, I have my passwords written down just in case, but I haven't forgotten how to do things I already know. It's not like that.
Have you been misplacing things, like keys or your phone, more often than usual?

No, not really. I'm pretty good about putting things back where they belong. My keys always go in the same dish by the door, so... no, I haven't been losing them or my phone. My memory is bothering me, like I said, but it's not that I'm walking around looking for things I just set down.
Do you have trouble remembering what happened in the correct order, like what you did first and what you did next?
No, I haven't noticed any trouble with that. I can usually keep straight what happened when. Like I said, it's just the memory thing... but no, the order of things seems fine.
Do you have trouble remembering things right after they happen, like conversations you just had?

No, I don't have that problem. If I just finish talking to someone, I... I know what we talked about. It doesn't just slip my mind the second we're done. So, no, I'd say I remember things fine right after they happen.
Do you have trouble recalling things that happened earlier in the day?
No, I can remember what I did this morning or this afternoon just fine. I don't seem to have any trouble with that.
Do you have trouble remembering things from one day to the next?
No, I don't have trouble with that either. I mean... if you ask me what I did yesterday, I can tell you. It doesn't just disappear overnight. So, no, my day-to-day memory is fine.
Do you find it hard to remember conversations or events from a few hours ago?

No, not really. I think that's pretty much like what you asked a minute ago about earlier in the day. If a conversation happened a few hours ago, I can remember it without any trouble. My memory for that sort of thing is just fine.
Do you have trouble remembering to do things in the future, like keeping appointments or taking medication?

Well, yes, actually. That's... that's kind of what brought me in. My head just feels really foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things. I'll forget what time an appointment is, or get dates wrong for the exhibits I help out with, or I'll forget which volunteer I've already called. It's just... things like that keep slipping my mind.
Do you find yourself often relying on reminders or notes to remember upcoming events or tasks?

No, I don't really use notes or reminders. I've always just kept track of things in my head. I suppose maybe I should start writing things down, given how much I've been mixing things up lately, but no, I haven't been doing that.
Do you often forget to do things that you had planned to do at a later time?

Well, I think that's basically what I was just talking about. Like I said, I've been mixing up my appointments and the dates for the exhibits. But if you mean other kinds of everyday plans... no, I haven't really noticed myself forgetting anything else. It's mostly just what I already told you.
Do you often forget to do things that you had planned to do at a specific time in the future?

No, I... I don't think so. I mean, like I said, it's just the appointments and the dates for the museum that I'm getting mixed up. I haven't really noticed myself forgetting to do things at an exact time, if that's what you mean. Just the things I already mentioned.
Do you find yourself forgetting things you intended to do, even if you didn't write them down or make a specific plan?

No, not really. I mean, it really is just those same few things I keep mentioning. I don't feel like I'm walking into rooms and forgetting why I'm there, or forgetting to pay a bill or something like that. It's just the dates and the appointments that are giving me trouble. Everything else seems fine.
Do you often forget to do things that you had planned to do, like taking medication or attending appointments, at the time you intended to do them?

Well, like I've been saying, it really is just those appointments I mentioned earlier. I don't take any medication right now, so that's not an issue. But yes, the appointments and the dates for the museum exhibits are the only things I'm forgetting when I'm supposed to do them. Other than that, my memory is fine.
